 The LADS SBU is seeking an Execution Production Chief Engineer (P5) to support technical execution for the LTAMDS (Lower Tier Air and Missile Defense Sensor) Production program. LTAMDS is a Raytheon franchise program delivering next‑generation radar capability with 360‑degree coverage to counter advanced threats, including hypersonic weapons. This role reports to the Production Chief Engineer and supports the LTAMDS Sub‑Strategic Business Unit (SSBU) Office of the Chief Engineer (OCE). The Execution Production CE assists with daily technical oversight across design, development, production, and delivery of LTAMDS production units and variants. This role focuses on disciplined execution, issue resolution, technical coordination, and maintaining alignment with program goals. This is an on‑site position located in Andover, MA.

 What You Will Do 
 Support execution of the product vision, technical strategy, and goals to meet program and customer milestones; assist in resolving technical conflicts.
 Ensure technical integrity and rigor across engineering execution for production efforts, meeting cost, schedule, and technical requirements.
 Serve as a technical point of contact for internal program leadership and customer engineering stakeholders as delegated by senior CE leadership.
 Contribute to new business activities, including technical inputs to proposals and influencing product roadmaps aligned with program planning.
 Drive continuous improvement within the production environment through participation in Failure Review Boards, FRACAS, and related activities.
 Coordinate technical engagement with subcontractors and partners to ensure product deliverables meet requirements.
 Lead and mentor teams of multi‑discipline engineers in resolving production and design issues.
 Travel domestically up to 25% to support hardware, test, supplier, and program activities; occasional international travel may be required.
 
 Qualifications You Must Have 
 Typically requires a Bachelor's degree in Science, Technology, Engineering, or Math (STEM) and a minimum of 10 years of prior relevant engineering experience.
 Experience supporting system development activities such as trade studies, requirements development, integration, test, or production support.
 Experience driving engineering execution, including developing work plans and coordinating cross‑functional activities.
 Experience leading engineering teams or task forces and supporting proposals or EAC activities.
 Experience managing or influencing work associated with multi‑million‑dollar budgets.
 Active and transferable Secret U.S. government issued security clearance is required prior to start date. U.S. citizenship is required as only U.S. citizens are eligible for a security clearance.
 
 Qualifications We Prefer 
 Degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or similar technical discipline.
 Experience with radar systems, radar subsystems, or related sensor components.
 Familiarity with formal Technical Data Package (TDP) release processes.
 Strong communication, technical writing, and presentation skills.
 Experience supporting or executing complex system design and development activities.
 Demonstrated experience across the product lifecycle including concept, design, integration, verification, and production.
 Experience working with Department of Defense and/or commercial customers, including requirements interpretation and stakeholder engagement.
 Ability to cultivate strong customer relationships to support program success.
 Experience with Engineering Risk & Opportunity management.
 Master’s degree in Engineering, Physics, or a related field.
 Experience supporting technical dispositions related to Export/Import (EXIM).
 
 What We Offer 
 Our values drive our actions, behaviors, and performance with a vision for a safer, more connected world. At RTX we value: Safety, Trust, Respect, Accountability, Collaboration, and Innovation.
 Relocation Eligibility– Relocation assistance is available.
 
 Learn More & Apply Now!

primaryBusiness:
Application close date:
Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed. 
 At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!    
 
 
This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities. 
 
 We are a team of collaborators, doers, and problem-solvers who are relentlessly committed to a culture of safety and operational excellence. This position will directly impact the history of space exploration and will require your commitment and detailed attention towards safe and repeatable space flight. Join us in lowering the cost of access to space and enabling Blue Origin’s vision of millions of people living and working in space to benefit Earth.
 The Sr. Manager, Test Operations role is responsible for leading the GEEx engine test stand near Van Horn, Texas. The Sr. Manager is a leader of passionate team of engineers and technicians who perform testing on our LH2 and LOX engine. The Sr. Manager works closely with all Blue Origin business units developing tests to develop and qualify in-space fluid and engine systems. The Sr Manager integrates with Test Operations senior leaders and support organizations to plan, prepare, and conduct test operations on a multi-cell test stand safely and efficiently. The Sr. Manager is responsible for effectively planning and leading all aspects of capital, overhead and labor budgets, and managing capital improvement projects. Effective communications and long term planning are vital to a successful Sr. Manager.
 We are looking for someone to apply their technical expertise, leadership skills, and commitment to quality to positively impact safe human spaceflight. Passion for our mission and vision is required!
 Management Responsibilities: 
 Lead the team at the Giant Engine Experiment (GEEx) test stand to include recruiting, training, coaching, mentoring, developing, and retaining talent by following and developing performance management processes.
 Promote teamwork, employee engagement, and good employee morale.
 Be an exemplar of Blue Leadership Principles, focusing on demonstrating operational excellence.
 Maintain employee training and development records.
 Demonstrate high standards in test operations and work cooperatively with a team of Responsible Engineers, Test Ops counterparts from other test stands, maintenance, Quality Specialists, and other team members to ensure requirements are met.
 Assist in the preparation of regular programmatic reports to help communicate inwards and outwards across the organization.
 Prepare quantitative strategic plans to ensure the targets are met, and leverage team skills and capabilities to implement and supervise progress against the plans.
 Lead capital, overhead, and labor budget planning and execution.
 Engineering Responsibilities: 
 Establish the technical direction for the GEEx test engineering team.
 Develop and implement test plans and procedures; perform subsequent data reduction and reviews.
 Lead the team in the design, planning, fabrication, installation, and operation of test facilities to the unique requirements from business unit customers
 Lead daily test operations, , direct technician work and coordinate with internal customers
 Understand and solve issues in fluid and instrumentation systems.
 Perform root cause analysis and failure investigations, lead implementation of corrective actions or continuous improvement projects
 Perform process hazard analyses (PHA)..
 Perform schedule and cost estimation and management.
 Find opportunities for safety improvements and cost savings.
 Align with and improve processes for test stand configuration management.
 Qualifications: 
 BS degree in engineering or related field
 3+ years as a manager or lead of a technical team
 12+ years in an operations environment in large industry, petrochemical, or aerospace facilities
 Strong background in fluid dynamics and thermodynamics
 Strong project management, and team leadership
 Outstanding technical and non-technical writing and verbal skills
 Demonstrated leadership in establishing a high performing safety culture
 Demonstrated habitual drive to correct errors at their root and not pass them downstream
 Demonstrated experience in setting high standards of performance and holding teams accountable
 Demonstrated effectiveness in implementing continuous improvement to improve processes, methods and practices
 Demonstrated effectiveness in conflict-resolution and an ability to bring a group to a decision
 Must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum
 Desired: 
 Demonstrated technical expertise in cryogenic test design and operations.
 Demonstrated technical expertise in liquid rocket engine test stand design, operation, and maintenance
 Previous experience operating in Process Safety Management (PSM) environment
 Knowledge of fabrication and integration processes, systems engineering and quality control practices
 MS in engineering or PMP certification
 


 Culture Statement 
 Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.

 Export Control Regulations 
 Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

 Background Check

 Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
 Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical
 
 Benefits 
 Benefits include:  Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
 Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)
 Paid Time Off:  Up to four (4) weeks per year based on weekly scheduled hours, and up to 14 company-paid holidays.

Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details.
